title: Adobe Forecasts 130% Surge in AI-Driven Retail Traffic During US Holiday Season
source_used: Yahoo Finance (own reporter Fiona Craig); Retail Dive for the release date
key_facts: Adobe forecasts traffic from AI tools to US retail sites will rise 130 percent this holiday season, against 4 percent for paid search and 17 percent for social media
AI-referred traffic is projected up 159 percent on Thanksgiving, 95 percent on Black Friday and 88 percent on Cyber Monday
Adobe expects US online holiday sales (1 Nov to 31 Dec) of $275.1 billion, up 6.7 percent; Cyber Week $47.5bn; Cyber Monday $15.1bn
In an Adobe survey of 5,000 consumers in July, 77 percent of AI shoppers said it raised purchase confidence and 69 percent said it made returns less likely
Retail Dive says the forecast was released on Monday 28 Sep 2026; Yahoo Finance published its article on 3 Oct
quote_evidence: Adobe forecasts that traffic from artificial intelligence tools to US retail websites will increase 130% during the upcoming holiday shopping season, exceeding expected growth from paid search and social media referrals.
Adobe expects US online sales between November 1 and December 31 to reach $275.1 billion, representing a 6.7% increase from the previous year.
why_it_matters_hint: Shoppers are letting AI assistants send them to stores, a shift retailers must now design for
notes: Yahoo Finance article carries its own byline (Fiona Craig), not a wire copy, so Yahoo Finance is the source. Event is five days old; Retail Dive (1 Oct) reported it earlier.
